security_audit.summary: Most code fence, PowerShell, Cobalt Strike, rootkit, and reconnaissance alerts are false positives because the skill is Markdown guidance for offline memory analysis. Confirmed risks remain for privileged live memory acquisition, direct /dev/mem and /proc/kcore access, temporary storage of RAM images, process-memory dumping, and credential extraction guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit authorization requirements and replace raw /dev/mem or /proc/kcore examples with safer acquisition tooling guidance.
Avoid writing full memory images to shared temporary paths. Recommend encrypted evidence storage with restrictive permissions.
Limit credential recovery steps to approved incident response and require redaction, need-to-know handling, and legal approval.
Label Cobalt Strike, rootkit, and YARA material as detection-only and remove any wording that suggests offensive use.

content.user_title: Analyze Memory Dumps with Forensic Workflows
content.value_statement: Memory investigations require careful acquisition, repeatable triage, and strong evidence handling. This skill guides authorized RAM capture analysis with Volatility, YARA, strings, and forensic checklists.
actual_capabilities: Lists memory acquisition options for Windows, Linux, macOS, and virtual machines.
Guides Volatility 3 setup, symbols, and plugin selection for common investigations.
Outlines workflows for process, network, registry, file, and timeline analysis.
Explains indicators for injection, rootkits, suspicious memory regions, and hidden processes.
Shows YARA, strings, and FLOSS methods for memory dump triage.
limitations: It provides guidance only; it does not acquire or analyze memory automatically.
Several commands require administrator or root privileges on approved systems.
Results depend on dump quality, operating system symbols, and supported Volatility plugins.
It may expose secrets, credentials, and personal data inside memory images.

use_cases.title: Triage a Compromised Endpoint
use_cases.description: Plan a focused memory analysis workflow for suspicious processes, network artifacts, persistence, and timeline clues.

use_cases.title: Investigate Malware in RAM
use_cases.description: Use process, VAD, YARA, string, and injection indicators to locate suspicious memory regions.

use_cases.title: Build a Forensics Lab Exercise
use_cases.description: Teach memory acquisition, Volatility plugin selection, artifact review, and evidence documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a safe memory forensics workflow for a Windows host. Ask for missing details before suggesting tools.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Volatility Plugins
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate triage of a memory image
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this memory dump scenario and choose Volatility 3 plugins for process, network, registry, and file artifact triage: [scenario].

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Injection
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an investigation checklist for suspected process injection in a Windows memory image, including validation steps and evidence notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Malware Analysis Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-stage malware memory analysis plan using Volatility 3, YARA scanning, strings extraction, and reporting checkpoints.

output_examples.input: I have a Windows memory image and suspect hidden malware.
output: Begin with process listings and process tree comparison.
Review hidden process indicators, suspicious memory protections, and network artifacts.
Document each finding with plugin output, timestamps, hashes, and validation notes.

output_examples.input: I need to scan a process dump for suspicious strings.
output: Create a working copy of the process dump before analysis.
Extract ASCII and Unicode strings, then separate URLs, IP addresses, paths, and commands.
Correlate suspicious strings with process metadata and related memory regions.

output_examples.input: I want a report outline for memory forensics findings.
output: Summarize scope, acquisition method, image hashes, and tool versions.
Group findings by process, network, persistence, credential exposure, and malware indicators.
State confidence, validation steps, impact, and recommended containment actions.

best_practices: Work on verified copies of memory images and preserve original hashes.
Run high-risk acquisition steps only with explicit authorization and documented scope.
Correlate memory findings with disk, endpoint, and network evidence before conclusions.
anti_patterns: Running live acquisition commands on systems outside your approved scope.
Saving full memory images in shared temporary directories or unencrypted storage.
Treating one plugin result as proof without cross-checking related artifacts.

faq.question: Does this skill run forensic tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example workflows. Users choose and run tools in their own environment.

faq.question: Which tools does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Volatility 3, memory acquisition tools, YARA, strings, and FLOSS.

faq.question: Can it help with malware analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers injected memory, suspicious processes, hidden modules, YARA scans, and string triage.

faq.question: Is administrator access required?
faq.answer: Some acquisition examples require administrator or root privileges. Use them only with explicit authorization.

faq.question: Does it handle chain of custody?
faq.answer: It includes practical guidance for hashing, documentation, and evidence handling during memory analysis.

faq.question: Can memory analysis expose sensitive data?
faq.answer: Yes. Memory images can contain credentials, keys, personal data, and confidential files.
